## Now

Wave 0 is LIVE VERIFIED. Wave 1 (#180) is exploratory semantic-scope work; implementation has not started.

## Solid

- Wave 0 delivered the Go proto contract as generated root `v0.1.120` / `ba7eda1f1833`, toolkit `encounter/v0.49.1`, and rpg-api#771; verification is recorded on [#192](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/issues/192#issuecomment-5206548237).
- Wave 1 runs structurally usable scope graphs without archetype cardinality/content/spawn enforcement. Missing semantic conventions are follow-up findings only where an existing surface permits; no diagnostics proto/API is added.
- rpg-api-protos#210 is a separate TypeScript/GitHub Release publication defect, not a Go gate. #772 (API update durability) and #885 (toolkit documentation) are separate.

## Next

Focused consistency review of PR #200; the prior independent review is invalidated. Do not cut Wave 1 implementation issues until this course correction is accepted.

## Pointers

- [#180](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/issues/180) · [PR #200](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/pull/200) · [#192 verification](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-project/issues/192#issuecomment-5206548237) · [rpg-api-protos#210](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-api-protos/issues/210)

## Lane: encounter reset (play/ family)

Axis two SHIPPED 2026-08-10: `play/record` v0.1.0 ([#907](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/pull/907)) and `play/intel` v0.1.0 ([#908](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/pull/908)) merged + tagged; docs PR [#906](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/pull/906) merged as ratification (triplets + execution addenda, incl. the `intel.Data` namesake clause). Family now: clock + intel + record, all v0.1.0, gorelease gates armed. `play/clock` v0.1.0 shipped 2026-08-09 (toolkit #901/#905/#902). Old `encounter` bugfix-only, delete-and-tag-pin agreed. **Next:** axis three — field (= `tools/spatial`, kept as-is per journey 051; Platform maintenance: toolkit [#909](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/issues/909) shipped independently as `tools/spatial/v0.8.0` via [PR #913](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/pull/913) (managed membership values, observer-only bus, race removed). [#910](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/issues/910) conservative housekeeping merged via [PR #915](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/pull/915) at `0fbcbca` after implementer/Copilot/CI/independent PASS: exactly 20 dead exports removed, offset+axial hex contracts and spatial-domain IDs preserved. Auto-tag misclassified the breaking pre-v1 cleanup as patch; erroneous `tools/spatial/v0.8.1` was removed before downstream consumption and corrected `tools/spatial/v0.9.0` now resolves through VCS + Go proxy to `0fbcbca` (workflow fix tracked as toolkit [#917](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/issues/917)). rpg-api [#789](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-api/issues/789) shipped to `dev` via [PR #790](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-api/pull/790) at `9556baf`: bounded spatial v0.9.0/core v0.11.0 bump, CI/Docker/focused race integrations green, and independent isolated full client game path PASS (Reference Tomb adjacent move `(0,-4,4)→(1,-5,4)`, browser event seq 1/2 + Redis persistence proven). #782 was notified to merge current `dev` and preserve these versions. Deferred until consumers exist: broader bus posture, per-channel occlusion, wire format) and interruption — **BUILT 2026-08-10: `play/interrupt` on toolkit [PR #914](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/pull/914), CI green (47 tests, all four gorelease gates), awaiting Kirk review/merge + tag `play/interrupt/v0.1.0`**; triplet + full execution addenda on [PR #912](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/pull/912) (merges as ratification — two in-build design amendments: Answer envelope = ownership transfer; R9 refinements incl. next_id-1 rejection). Ledger of open windows; custody-not-execution; no timeouts v1; Shield fixture scene proven in AC1; OA-with-option first production consumer (playable roster monk/fighter/rogue/barbarian, **level 1 only, leveling unimplemented** — Protection fighting style also available at L1). Bus evaluation ratified as journey 052 (toolkit PR #911, in review). **DECIDED 2026-08-10:** the new composition is born **inside the rulebook** (dnd5e encounter, not a generic package — generic extraction is a shelf a second rulebook pays for); lead wave = the **free-roam exploration encounter** (outcome visible in action; composes clock+spatial+intel+record, no suspendable resolutions needed) — composition brainstormed same day — **triplet on toolkit [PR #918](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/pull/918)** (rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter as its OWN module; ambient free-roam ground state; members exit / encounters close; declared endings + per-member carry-forward, quest layer above; activity-pumped ticks, no background process; laws C1–C8; AC1 = the tomb watch). **BUILT 2026-08-11: toolkit [PR #921](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/pull/921)** (172 tests; the tomb-watch scene green end-to-end; review trail incl. an Opus persistence cycle — 6 majors fixed: snapshot determinism, a trust-boundary panic, discriminating rejections; awaiting Kirk review/merge + tag `rulebooks/dnd5e/encounter/v0.1.0`). #918 ratifies alongside (full addenda). Next after merge: rpg-api wires the free-roam encounter (the clock.Tick consumer finally lands); the combat wave rides Platform's #916. The **resolution axis** is handed to Platform as toolkit [#916](https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/issues/916) (wave 1 = suspendable MOVEMENT resolution + OA-with-option via play/interrupt, design-first, auto-OA compatibility mode; suspendable attack phases = wave 2 when casters arrive; explicitly NOT events-module work — journey 052 stance). rpg-api's clock.Tick free-roam consumer rides the composition wave. Deep record: toolkit `docs/journey/051-*`, `docs/ideas/play/{clock,intel,record,interrupt}/`.

Two axes on every item (since July 20, 2026):

- **Feature** — what part of the game: Party Assembles, Class Kits, The Dungeon, Game Screen, Capstone, Shelf (parked/backlog), Infra (tooling, CI/deploy, QA harnesses).
- **Team** — who owns it: UI/UX, Platform, Assets, Cross-team (Kirk-level milestones and playtest gates). **Empty Team = needs triage.**

Ownership boundaries:
- **Platform**: rules engine, api, protos, deployment — and wire-and-state correctness end to end, including the client half of stream/reconnect/snapshot plumbing in rpg-dnd5e-web.
- **UI/UX**: screens, HUD, UX flows — presentation and interaction once state arrives.
- **Assets**: asset pipeline plus 3D client seams (model loading, props rendering, animation playback, char-creation appearance).

Two structural drift couplings survive PR #779's condition-provenance work (https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/pull/779, gate findings #1–#2) — each is a place where a future addition silently leaks a build-time condition into `ActiveConditions` with **zero failing tests**:

1. **Monster mirror, missing-entry direction**: `monstertraits.AllTraitRefs()` hand-mirrors `LoadJSON`'s dispatch switch (documented as such — the switch has no enumerable registry). A 5th trait added to the switch but forgotten in `AllTraitRefs` loads fine, enters `Data.Conditions`, and leaks into snapshots. The in-PR tripwire (construct-each-trait-via-LoadJSON → assert ref ∈ AllTraitRefs) catches phantom entries, not missing ones. Full closure: make `LoadJSON` dispatch from a map-based registry that `AllTraitRefs` derives from — one source of truth.
2. **Character-side source coupling**: `StructurallyPermanentConditionRefs` derives from `compileConditions`' *current* sources (class grants + fighting styles). If `compileConditions` ever gains a new build-time source (race/background/feat conditions — none exist today, gate-verified), the derivation silently under-covers. No test binds the derivation to `compileConditions`' actual source list; the golden list only pins the derivation's output. Closure idea: have `compileConditions` and the derivation share a single "build-time condition sources" enumeration, or a test that walks a fully-built draft of each class and asserts every attached condition ref is classified permanent.

## Why not in #779

Both need small refactors of authoring-side structures (trait registry; source enumeration) — judged scope creep for the provenance fix and documented honestly there instead. This issue is the "next contributor gets a failing test instead of a silent leak" completion.

## Related

rpg-toolkit#778 (the provenance design), rpg-api#651 (the consumer this protects), toolkit#777 (same family: registry structures with implicit contracts).

Found during live verification of #444 (resume-after-refresh). Every new character creation currently gets stuck at the Ability Scores step: `Confirm Ability Scores` / `Begin Adventure!` never enables even after all 6 scores show "Assigned" in the UI.

## Root cause

`src/character/creation/sections/AbilityScoresSection.tsx`'s `useAbilityScoreRolls` (`src/api/diceHooks.ts`) always submits `UpdateAbilityScoresRequest` with the `roll_assignments` oneof branch, referencing roll IDs that look client-generated (`roll-<timestamp>-<random>`, e.g. `roll-_1784334707968372023_f48d1a74`). These were never registered server-side via `RollAbilityScores` — clicking the pre-populated Standard Array numbers (15/14/13/12/10/8) directly assigns them to abilities without ever calling `RollAbilityScores` first.

Server response confirms this precisely:
```
grpc-message: NOT_FOUND: failed to get dice roll session (tried both player ID and draft ID): NOT_FOUND: failed to get dice session: NOT_FOUND: dice session not found
```

`UpdateAbilityScoresRequest` actually supports a second, simpler path that sidesteps this entirely:
```proto
message UpdateAbilityScoresRequest {
  string draft_id = 1;
  oneof scores_input {
    AbilityScores ability_scores = 2;      // <- direct values, no roll session needed
    RollAssignments roll_assignments = 3;  // <- what the UI currently always uses
  }
}
```
Confirmed working via `grpcurl` using the `ability_scores` direct-value branch — the draft immediately shows `hasAbilityScores: true`, `completionPercentage: 100`, and `FinalizeDraft` succeeds cleanly.

## Suggested fix

In Standard Array (and likely point-buy) mode, `AbilityScoresSection` should call `UpdateAbilityScores` with the direct `ability_scores` field instead of `roll_assignments`. The `roll_assignments` path should only be used when the player actually rolled dice via `RollAbilityScores` first (Roll mode).

## Impact

Currently blocks finishing character creation for every new character via the UI. On merged main (rpg-api 65bc7ad, toolkit encounter v0.29.1): **MoveEntity silently no-ops in encounters created via the lobby's StartEncounter RPC** — the RPC returns success, but the entity never moves; the `entityMoved` stream event carries a single zero-length step (`actualPath: [{}]`), i.e. the toolkit treats every step as prevented. The identical move on the identical character in a devseed-created encounter succeeds.

Found by the reconnect-fidelity wave's closing playtest (umbrella #649) — it fully blocks the wave's headline verification (and any lobby-created fight at all).

## Repro (evidence in /home/kirk/personal/rpg-api/playtest-evidence-reconnect/)

1. `go run ./cmd/devseed --fixture=wave-3-barbarian` (char-bob) → create lobby as bob → ready → StartEncounter → FREE_ROAM, bob at {0,0,0}.

3. Control: `devseed --fixture=wave-3-barbarian --mode=free_roam --encounter-id=isolation-test` (same char-bob, direct Redis write) → identical grpcurl move succeeds, position updates.

Ruled out: geometry (target hex in bob's own revealed set, open 20×20 room, no walls nearby, goblins at R:-13/-16), browser/injection artifacts (grpcurl repro), the two predicted wave edges (toolkit#691 window, DurationRounds — this is upstream of both).

## Why now (regression window)

The wave-1 closing playtest (2026-07-16) verified movement in lobby-created encounters extensively. Landed on the StartEncounter/Move path since: rpg-api#650/#652 (spawn-engine adoption — goblins now genuinely room-registered at engine positions; PositionOracle; encounter bump v0.26→v0.28) and #655 (v0.29.1). Playtest driver's working hypothesis from move_entity.go's own comments: the hydration-cascade / WithCharacterData movement-resolver wiring (#684/#689 area) differing between the StartEncounter path and devseed's direct write — unconfirmed.

## The uncomfortable question for the retro

Every gate passed and the full -race suite is green on main — including integration tests that move entities in StartEncounter-created encounters. Whatever differs between those tests and the live RPC path (resolver wiring? hydration entry point? proto-vs-direct verb?) is a coverage hole to name precisely as part of the fix.

## Ask

Root-cause, fix at the honest layer (if the toolkit's Move is correctly refusing based on state the api mis-assembled, the fix is api-side; if a toolkit seam mis-handles the assembled state, issue there), and add a test that exercises the ACTUAL failing path (StartEncounter via RPC → MoveEntity via RPC) so this class can't pass silently again. The closing playtest re-runs after this lands.
","title":"MoveEntity silently no-ops in StartEncounter-created encounters — every step 'prevented', works in devseed encounters","number":656,"repository":"KirkDiggler/rpg-api","url":"https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-api/issues/656"},"feature":"Shelf","id":"PVTI_lAHOAASbwc4Bcj4vzgzQudw","linked pull requests":["https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-api/pull/657"],"repository":"https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-api","status":"Done","team":"Platform","title":"MoveEntity silently no-ops in StartEncounter-created encounters — every step 'prevented', works in devseed encounters"},{"content":{"type":"Issue","body":"## What

A refused/truncated move is **silent on the wire**: `MoveEntity` returns RPC success with a truncated (possibly zero-length) `actualPath` and no reason. The client can detect "I didn't move" only by noticing the empty path — it cannot tell *why* (wall, room bounds, movement budget), and the player sees nothing happen with no explanation.

PR #657 (https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-api/pull/657) removed the worst *trigger* (corner spawn made half of all first moves refuse), but the behavior class remains for every legitimate refusal: walk into a wall → silence.

## Layering (why this is two issues in two repos)

- **Toolkit first** (rpg-toolkit#757 is the tracked home): `Move`'s truncation is currently reason-blind — out-of-bounds, wall, and budget all truncate identically. The toolkit must distinguish refusal reasons before anyone can surface them.
- **Then rpg-api** (this issue): once the toolkit returns a reason, project it onto the wire — either fields on the `entityMoved` event / `MoveEntityResponse` (proto addition, additive) or a distinct refusal event — so the client can render "blocked by wall" vs "not enough movement."
- **Then web**: render the refusal (shake, toast, path-preview truncation cue — product call).

## Why it matters soon

The reconnect wave's closing playtest — and any real player — hits "click a hex, nothing happens, no feedback" the first time they path at a wall. Dungeon wave 2 (doors, multi-room) multiplies blocked-path interactions.

## Ask

Sequence behind rpg-toolkit#757: when the toolkit grows refusal reasons, add the wire projection here (additive proto change per the deprecate-don't-delete policy — new fields only). Until then this issue is the tracked home for the "silent refusal on the wire" symptom so playtests can reference it instead of re-filing.

Condition badges **never survive a reconnect**: `EncounterView.tsx`'s `onSnapshotDelivered` handler (~lines 137-176) builds entity state from the snapshot but only reads position/HP/AC/type — it never reads `entity.statusEffects`. The `entityStatuses` map that drives the rendered badge (~line 285/409) is populated only by the live `onStatusApplied` handler (~line 234-236). So a reconnecting client shows no badges regardless of what the server sends.

Server side verified working during the reconnect wave's closing playtest: the raw `StreamEncounter` snapshot (grpcurl, bypassing the client) carries `statusEffects: [{module: dnd5e, type: conditions, id: raging}]` on the raging character — rpg-api#655's projection is correct on the wire. Full trace with code pointers: `rpg-api/playtest-evidence-reconnect/bug-badge-never-hydrates.txt`.

This is the third instance of the same disease (dead `player_id` write, unconsumed `InitiativeRolled`): a wire field with no client consumer.

## Fix

In the snapshot handler, seed `entityStatuses` from each entity's `statusEffects` (same shape `onStatusApplied` produces — Source ref parsed the same way), replacing (not merging into) any stale pre-refresh state. Live `StatusApplied`/`StatusRemoved` events continue to mutate it afterward — snapshot seeds, stream updates, one map.

## Verify

Unit: feed a snapshot with statusEffects → assert entityStatuses populated; feed empty → cleared. Live: rage → act → refresh → 🔥 badge present (the reconnect wave's headline scenario — this issue BLOCKS the wave's close). Also observe whether the reconnected badge differs from the live one in duration display (expected: no DurationRounds on snapshot badges — cosmetic, tracked on the wave umbrella).
","title":"Snapshot statusEffects never hydrate entityStatuses — condition badges cannot survive reconnect","number":462,"repository":"KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web","url":"https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/issues/462"},"feature":"Shelf","id":"PVTI_lAHOAASbwc4Bcj4vzgzSCNw","linked pull requests":["https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web/pull/463"],"repository":"https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-dnd5e-web","status":"Done","team":"Platform","title":"Snapshot statusEffects never hydrate entityStatuses — condition badges cannot survive reconnect"},{"content":{"type":"Issue","body":"## What

An **unconscious (0 HP) character can take full normal turns** — observed live in the reconnect wave's closing playtest: a downed PC got a full economy round (Action 1 / Bonus 1 / Reaction 1 / Movement 30) and successfully attacked, landing a killing blow — then in a LATER round while still unconscious had all-zero economy. Both halves are wrong and they're inconsistent with each other:

1. Under 5e rules an unconscious creature is incapacitated — no actions, no movement; its turns are death saves.
2. The zero-economy round shows some path does gate the downed PC, but not the same one every round — whatever seeds/refreshes turn economy disagrees with itself about unconscious actors across rounds.

## Evidence

Playtest run 2026-07-18 (evidence in rpg-api/playtest-evidence-reconnect/): bob at 0 HP received "Round N — char-bob's turn" with full economy, attacked goblin-1 successfully; subsequent unconscious round showed 0/0/0/0.

## Related

- toolkit#772 (TPK never ends the encounter) — same death-handling family, confirmed live in the same playtest (single-player death left the encounter in TURN_BASED forever). The death.go machinery (death saves, wave 2.10 seats-stay) presumably intends unconscious ≠ acting; the turn-advance/economy-seed path isn't consulting it.
- Wave 2's boss-room shape makes downed-PC handling a designed scenario, not an edge.

## Ask

Decide the unconscious-turn contract (skip turn entirely + death-save prompt vs auto-pass) and make the economy seeding consistent with it every round. Pin with a test: 0 HP actor's turn → no actions available, turn advances (or death-save flow), across multiple rounds.
","title":"Unconscious (0 HP) character takes full normal turns — inconsistently across rounds","number":781,"repository":"KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit","url":"https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/issues/781"},"feature":"The Dungeon","id":"PVTI_lAHOAASbwc4Bcj4vzgzSCOI","linked pull requests":["https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/pull/783"],"repository":"https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit","status":"Todo","team":"Platform","title":"Unconscious (0 HP) character takes full normal turns — inconsistently across rounds"},{"content":{"type":"Issue","body":"## What

The **first NPC turn after combat entry stalls indefinitely** (30+ seconds, no server log activity) — reproduced in BOTH runs of the reconnect wave's closing playtest (2026-07-18). A browser refresh (which reconnects `StreamEncounter`) reliably un-stalls it, and the round then completes normally; subsequent NPC turns are fine.

## Observed

- Combat entry via a sighted Move → TURN_BASED, initiative rolled with a goblin first.
- Goblin's turn: nothing happens. No NPC action events, no log lines, 30+ seconds.
- Refresh → reconnect → the goblin immediately acts and the encounter proceeds.

## Why the reconnect un-stalls it (hypothesis, unverified)

The un-stall-on-reconnect signature points at the NPC drive kick being tied to stream lifecycle rather than the mode-transition itself — the #638 single-flight NPC kick (`drive_npc.go`) area. If the kick that should fire on combat entry is missed (raced? subscribed-after-publish?) the encounter waits until the next kick source — which a fresh stream connect apparently provides. The prior #636 fix covered NPC-first *seeding*; this presents as the combat-entry variant.

## Evidence

Both playtest runs' timelines in `rpg-api/playtest-evidence-reconnect/`; encounter ids in the run notes. Reliably reproducible: enter combat with a goblin winning initiative, don't refresh, watch it hang.

## Ask

Root-cause the missing first kick on the FREE_ROAM→TURN_BASED transition and make the drive kick deterministic on combat entry (not dependent on a client reconnect). Add a test: combat entry with NPC first in initiative → NPC turn events arrive without any stream reconnect.
","title":"First NPC turn after combat entry stalls until a client reconnects — drive kick missing on mode transition","number":659,"repository":"KirkDiggler/rpg-api","url":"https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-api/issues/659"},"feature":"The Dungeon","id":"PVTI_lAHOAASbwc4Bcj4vzgzSCOo","linked pull requests":["https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-api/pull/661"],"repository":"https://github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-api","status":"Done","team":"Platform","title":"First NPC turn after combat entry stalls until a client reconnects — drive kick missing on mode transition"},{"content":{"type":"Issue","body":"## Goal (wave = observable behavior)

**Death behaves like a rule, not a soft-lock.** In the real game: a downed (0 HP) PC stops taking normal turns; when the whole party drops, the encounter ENDS with a defeat outcome (mirror of the existing all-hostiles-defeated victory), the end-of-combat sweeps run for everyone (conditions removed, exhaustion cleared — #752/#767 machinery), and a subsequent encounter starts clean. Verified by MCP playtest: lose a fight on purpose → defeat announced → refresh lands Home (no ghost fight) → next fight starts with full economy.

Kirk's framing at the reconnect-wave retro: "no sense rushing off to the next thing if we are leaving tech debt behind."

## Members

- #772 — TPK never ends the encounter (`checkEncounterEnd`'s only predicate is zero monsters). **Confirmed live** 2026-07-18: solo PC died, encounter looped the corpse's turns forever.
- #781 — Unconscious (0 HP) PC takes full normal turns, inconsistently across rounds (full economy one round, zero another; landed a killing blow while unconscious).
- Design decisions owned by this wave (design-first before code): the encounter-end outcome taxonomy (victory/defeat now; flee later — decide the shape once), and the unconscious-turn contract (auto-skip vs death-save flow — death-save machinery exists in death.go; decide what wave-appropriate minimum is honest without faking rules we haven't built).

## Consumer surface (expected small)

`EncounterEndedEvent` already reaches the wire with a reason (the victory path logs "all_hostiles_defeated") — defeat should reuse the same shape with a new reason value: expected zero proto changes, small api/web touches only if the log/summary rendering needs the new reason string. If design finds otherwise, say so before implementing.

The ability-score rolling contract diverges from its implementation, in both directions (found during web#460's root-cause):

1. **The documented flow is unimplemented at the gRPC layer**: `CharacterService.RollAbilityScores(draft_id)` — the proto's own inline docs describe its server-issued IDs ("roll_1, roll_2, etc." — actually idGen-generated, so the doc is wrong in detail too) as the intended source for `RollAssignments` — returns `Unimplemented` (rpg-api `internal/handlers/dnd5e/v1alpha1/character/handler.go:749-755`). An orchestrator method backing it EXISTS (`orchestrator.go:788-822`, draft-ID-keyed session via the dice service) but is unreachable via gRPC; the web client's hook for it is likewise dead code (zero callers). So wiring "rolled stats" is mostly plumbing the handler to existing orchestration, not a build-from-scratch.
2. **The enforced flow is undocumented**: `UpdateAbilityScores`'s `roll_assignments` branch actually validates against the *generic Dice Service* session (`SetAbilityScoresFromRolls`, orchestrator.go:455-538 — session keyed by `draft.Data.PlayerID` + context `ability_scores`, with a fallback lookup by draft ID). ## Context

web#460's fix sidesteps all of this by submitting direct values via the `ability_scores` oneof branch (the UI is a standard-array picker; no dice UX exists since commit e2a504c removed the roll buttons). So nothing is broken for the current game after that fix — this issue is about the contract debt left behind.

## Ask (decide once)

Either **implement** the documented flow — `RollAbilityScores` orchestrated over the dice service (draft-scoped session, auth-derived identity so the seam closes) — as the future "rolled stats" mode's server half; or **retire** it per the deprecation policy (deprecate the RPC + `RollAssignments` docs pointing at the real mechanism). Don't leave a documented-but-Unimplemented RPC as the contract's stated intent. If "rolled stats" is a product direction (it's a classic D&D feel), implementing properly is the better half of this fork — but that's Kirk's call.
